narrativeSummary: Five weeks that moved the portfolio from dependency management to execution. NEXUS exited hypercare clean and is the first solid green since Q1. ATLAS chose its SLA over its customer-count milestone — the July uptime breach was contained by rate-limiting onboarding, then structurally fixed by the circuit breaker on Jul 31, at the cost of four frozen weeks on M7. PULSE finally closed FlowEngine on Aug 7, thirteen days late and $1.38M into dual-run, but off red for the first time this year. HORIZON delivered soft GA on time after buying back its beta slip with a dedicated onboarding engineer, and now waits on Apple. The real story is SHIELD: 100 controls closed on time on Jul 15, then the auditor failed 3 of them on Jul 16 for having no operating history — which forced into the open a contradiction the program had carried since kickoff. The board's Aug 31 mandate was never achievable as certification; it was always audit-readiness, with the Type II report landing Dec 15. Naming that (DR-014) cost one uncomfortable board conversation and removed a structural lie from the portfolio. At the boundary, SPARK M2 is due tomorrow at 88%.
